plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of competitors' bids or strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Since my value is $49 (the maximum possible), bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit and ensures I capture the full surplus when I win, since I only pay what the second-highest bidder bid.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding my actual value of $7 maximizes my expected profit—I won't overpay if I win, and I won't miss profitable opportunities by underbidding. There's no benefit to shading my bid up or down in this format, regardless of what other bidders do. I'll bid exactly my value.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what other bidders do. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth. If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. With my value at $9, I should bid exactly $9 to ensure optimal expected profit.
